title: Trees worldwide recorded a mystery blast in 774 🌲
subject: sun
description:
Do you think our power grid could survive a storm like 774? 👇

In 2012, Fusa Miyake's team found a sudden carbon-14 spike in Japanese cedar rings from 774 AD. The same signal appears in trees across the world and in Antarctic ice. The leading explanation is an extreme solar storm, far stronger than the 1859 Carrington Event, though some researchers argue the cause is still unclear.

Sources: Miyake et al., "A signature of cosmic-ray increase in AD 774-775 from tree rings in Japan", Nature (2012); Usoskin et al., Astronomy & Astrophysics (2013); Wikipedia, "774-775 carbon-14 spike"; Live Science, "Mystery of 'Miyake events' deepens" (Benjamin Pope, University of Queensland; Zhang et al., Proceedings of the Royal Society A); Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, entry for 774.
tags: what if a solar storm hit today

scenes.text: Trees from Japan to New Zealand carry the same scar.
In 2012, Fusa Miyake's team found it in Japanese cedar rings from 774: a carbon-14 jump 20 times normal.
Germany, Russia, America: the same spike, and in Antarctic ice too.
That year, England's Anglo-Saxon Chronicle described a red crucifix in the sky after sunset.
The leading explanation is a solar storm 80 times stronger than the 1859 Carrington Event.
Astrophysicist Benjamin Pope says one today would wreck satellites, internet cables and power transformers.
